---
title: "Permanent plots"
---

The MELANOBS network is made up of permanent plots of 1 ha (100 m × 100 m). In each plot, every stem with a diameter at breast height (DBH, measured 1.3 m above the ground) of at least 10 cm is identified botanically, measured and mapped. This includes trees as well as palms, tree ferns, pandanus and other growth forms. Each individual carries a tag with a unique number, and the point of measurement is marked with paint so that every census measures the stem at exactly the same height.

A voucher specimen of each species recorded in the plots has been collected and deposited in the [herbaria](herbaria.qmd) of the region.

Additional measurements are made in and around the plots, including tree height (H) and wood density. They are used to calibrate local height–diameter (H–DBH) allometries and to estimate above-ground biomass and carbon stocks.

The protocol follows the international standards of the [ForestPlots.net](https://forestplots.net) network.

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/map.R")
melanobs_map(show = "plots")
p <- read_plots()
knitr::kable(data.frame(paste0("[", p$site, "](plots/", p$slug, ".qmd)"),
                        p$island, p$country, coord(p$lat), coord(p$lon)),
             col.names = c("Plot", "Island", "Country", "Latitude", "Longitude"))
```
